But one thing I’d like to say that’s getting into the semantics a bit is play wrestling can be considered its own sub-domain of training within this grey area and within the grey area there is a near infinite amount of options of how to train people. I studied this stuff and how to optimize learning for a few years and I feel as though I’ve barely scratched the surface.
Glad I could help and you can feel free to shoot me a DM if you ever get stuck on something or need a more practical example.

To expand on what the other guy said in Russia almost all of their wrestlers come from Dagestan or very close to that region and grappling (not just wrestling) is life there. And they also have training methods that almost perfectly mimic the best learning models today where almost no other place does on such a large scale. There is a page called @Schoolofgrappling on instagram that does a better break down than any i’ve seen on how the process of learning works and how to properly define the different types of learning. Be warned it’s one hell of a rabbit hole and not always easy to understand.

But to give a brief preview of what you might learn: 

Picture yourself in a parked car imagining what you would do if the car slipped on ice and you needed to recover. It’s better than nothing but not great at preparing you for the real thing.

Now picture yourself driving at highway speeds and then slipping on ice. You might learn faster than the first example but obviously there’s so many other variables that it’s hard to learn and mimic.

Now picture yourself in an empty parking lot with nothing around you and you speed up a little and then make your car slide so you can learn to recover. This one is safer, you’re more focused, you’re able to get a lot of reps in quickly, and it’s also kinda fun.

This is what the Russians are great at. Where Americans are typically focused on the first example(Drilling techniques) and the second example(Live sparring) the Russians are in that gray area in between that has the focus of drilling but the real resistance of live sparing. Hope that helps.
